title: introduce-session-cursor-primitives-first-class-resume-and-retry-builder-across-sdks
author: Priya Raman
release_notes:
- Add SessionCursor primitive to Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for explicit resume semantics and safer lifecycle management.
- Introduce ResumeToken surface and Cursor.resume() for deterministic continuation across reconnects.
- New RetryBuilder DSL for configurable backoff profiles and circuit hints; replaces ad-hoc backoff config in several places.
- Performance tweaks in TypeScript stream pump and Go iterator to reduce allocations in hot paths.
- Version bumps: python -> 2.2.0, typescript -> 1.8.0, go -> 1.5.0
description:
Motivation: Several customers and internal teams reported fragile resume behavior when streams are interrupted mid-session and an inconsistent retry surface across SDKs made cross-language troubleshooting harder. This PR introduces a lightweight SessionCursor primitive (first-class in Py/TS/Go) and a small RetryBuilder DSL to unify retry/backoff ergonomics across SDKs.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Added SessionCursor API in each SDK: Cursor.open(), Cursor.next_chunk(), Cursor.pause(), Cursor.resume(resume_token) and Cursor.close(). ResumeToken is an opaque string produced by Cursor.pause() that captures minimal resume state (server-side pointer + checksum). The cursor API intentionally exposes a small surface to encourage deterministic resume behavior without leaking runtime internals. Introduced RetryBuilder to construct retry profiles (preset: conservative, default, aggressive) and to attach circuit-breaker hints and max-total-duration. The SDKs now surface a RetryPolicy object on client constructors to make it simple to configure a retry strategy for streaming vs. unary calls. Kept backward compatibility by providing a compatibility shim: client.stream() still works and automatically adapts to Cursor where appropriate.

Commits included (high-level): * 9c1b4d9: introduce session cursor primitive and tests (py/ts/go) * 4a7e2bb: add ResumeToken encoder/decoder and cross-sdk format spec * b6f2a01: implement RetryBuilder DSL and attach to client constructors * e2f98c7: TS: optimize stream pump to reuse chunk buffers and reduce GC pressure * d3a7f12: Go: iterator allocation reduction and docs * f8b5aa0: docs: add guide (migrating from stream to cursor) and release notes * 2c4b091: test: add integration test for resume across reconnects and simulated partial payloads

Files changed (high-level): - sdk/python/redwood/session.py, sdk/python/tests/test_cursor_resume.py - sdk/typescript/src/cursor.ts, sdk/typescript/src/retry_builder.ts, sdk/typescript/tests/cursor.spec.ts - sdk/go/cursor.go, sdk/go/retry_builder.go, sdk/go/cursor_integration_test.go - docs/guides/session_cursor.md - examples/cursor_resume_demo/* - package.json & pyproject.toml & go.mod version bumps and changelogs

Review thread (abridged): - Diego: "API looks sensible, question about the opacity of ResumeToken: do we ever need a version field?" Priya: "Yes, added a 1-byte format version in the token; decoder rejects unknown versions and falls back to full stream restart. See encoder change in commit 4a7e2bb." - Maya: "Please add explicit docs on semantics when server evicts state (token invalidation)." Priya: "Added a section in docs/guides/session_cursor.md and a test simulating token rejection and graceful fallback." - Evan: "Can TS buffer reduction change regress older Node LTS?" Priya: "Benchmark run included; pump path empirically neutral on Node 14/16/18; added feature flag to opt into reusing buffers in older runtimes." - Diego (final): "Approve after small naming nit addressed." Priya: "Addressed, renamed Cursor.resume_token -> ResumeToken per review."

CI: Initial run showed one flaky integration test failing (cursor-resume flaky under simulated packet drop). Re-ran the integration suite with increased timeouts and deterministic RNG seed; all checks passed. CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, lint: pass, benchmarks: informational (no regression).

Compatibility and migration notes: Existing stream users are unaffected; stream() continues to work. Migrating to Cursor offers deterministic resume/resilience and explicit lifecycle management. ResumeToken invalidation is a possible failure mode; SDKs now expose a clear error type (ResumeTokenInvalid) and recommend calling client.stream() fallback upon token rejection.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show 8-12% lower per-token allocation overhead for TypeScript streaming hot path and 5-7% improvement in Go iterator throughput in local benchmarks. Python changes are low-level, focused on ergonomics and testability, not micro-optimizations.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and green CI. Follow-ups: 1) Backport cursor to the v1.x SDK branch for enterprise clients (planned). 2) Add a server-side opt-in to persist resume pointers beyond short-term cache. 3) Expose RetryBuilder presets in SDK config UI on the Console (tracking ENG-1975).
notes: Backported patch queued for v1.x branch; docs site updated; example demo added to examples/ and quickstart updated with a cursor resume snippet.
